_about: Fabrication limits for parts WE make (not bought ones, like a mesh sheet). The process is resin 3D printing (the tool/master) plus hot embossing into COC/COP; we no longer laser-cut anything. tools/check_chip_spec.py compares fabricated feature sizes (in um) with these and only ever WARNS: fabrication limits never block the design. check_chip_spec reads two keys, laser_kerf_um and min_embossed_feature_um, and takes the larger numeric one as the minimum; they are kept under these names so the checker keeps working. laser_kerf_um is now MEANINGLESS (no laser cutter in the process): it is deliberately set to the same value as min_embossed_feature_um only so the checker has a number; do not read it as a kerf. min_embossed_feature_um = 200, the floor agreed in contracts/blocks.json fabrication_floors.min_open_channel_mm (0.2 mm) converted to um; that is the source of truth, change it there first. These are agreed floors, not yet measured on our printer and press. The other agreed floors are mirrored in fabrication_floors_mm for reference only (the checker reads them from contracts/blocks.json, not from here). display_scale: how much bigger cad/export_display_model.py makes the printed display model.
